# infrawrench_cost_forecast (Resource)

A named forecast on an `infrawrench_cost_report`: the plan you compare the automatic trend forecast against.

A forecast starts from a baseline, either the report's spend trend or, when `driver_metric_id` is set, the report's projected spend per unit of a business metric multiplied by that metric's forecasted values. Scenario models are then applied in the order listed, each to the line the previous ones produced. Every forecast carries a low/expected/high band from the least-squares prediction interval; scenario models shift the band rather than widening it.

At least one of `scenario_model_ids` and `driver_metric_id` must be set: without either the forecast is the automatic one, which every report already has. A scenario model a forecast names cannot be deleted until the forecast stops naming it.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cost_report_id` (String) The report whose scope the forecast projects. Changing it replaces the forecast: the route is nested under the report, so there is nothing to move.
- `name` (String) Shown in the report's Forecasts view, 1–120 characters, unique on the report.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free text, at most 500 characters.
- `driver_metric_id` (String) An `infrawrench_business_metric` id. When set, the baseline is the report's projected spend per unit of the metric times the metric's forecasted values; days with no forecasted value fall back to the trend. Forecasted values are data, entered in the app, by CSV, or over the API, and are not managed here.
- `is_default` (Boolean) Make this the report's default forecast: the one its Forecasts view opens on and the forecasted-costs read returns. Setting it clears any other default on the report, so set it on at most one forecast per report or the two will take turns on every apply. Defaults to `false`.
- `scenario_model_ids` (List of String) `infrawrench_scenario_model` ids, in priority order (first applied first), at most 10, each at most once. Order matters only for org-wide percentage changes: a later model's percentage also scales the amounts an earlier one added.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Server-assigned forecast id. Import addresses it as `<cost_report_id>/<id>`, because the forecast's own id is not enough to build its URL.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A forecast hangs off its report, so the forecast id alone cannot build a
# URL. The address is <cost_report_id>/<forecast_id>.
terraform import infrawrench_cost_forecast.plan 7b8c9d0e-1f2a-3b4c-5d6e-7f8a9b0c1d2e/5c6d7e8f-9a0b-1c2d-3e4f-5a6b7c8d9e0f
```
